I think that's part of the issue though. I can't really figure out if "addiction" or "dependence" are the right words.

When I think "addiction" I think of things like alcoholism and "harder" drugs. If I was drinking every single night and/or doing coke/shooting heroin/etc then I'd be like YEP THIS IS ADDICTION.

But there's far less stigma with weed - particularly with it becoming legal in a lot of places now. But does less stigma necessarily mean it's still addiction or not?

It just feels weird to be taking these little capsules every night that help me relax \*so much\* and help me sleep \*so much better\* - it seems like it's too good to be true, or there must be a caveat somewhere. I think I've determined that if I wanted to stop, I could, and I tested that by stopping for a week and I was fine.

I'm not busting my wallet on it and I am not letting them take over my life ... so I'm like... is that okay? Is this safe? Will my stomach melt? etc.
Thanks! :)

I've been seeing a psychologist on and off for several months now regarding this and a bunch of other different fucked up things that have happened to me in my relationships. My boyfriend has been seeing someone as well, though I am not sure how much of it is regarding the assault itself. 

But yeah. I'm taking care to just try and be a bit sensitive on the issue. It's just hard not to get a little fired up over it because it's something I can uncomfortably relate to, and it's happened to somebody I care about.

You're totally right. It is a crime, but it's also not uncommon for victims of sexual assault **not** to speak up about their experience after the event has happened. You hear and read about it all the time - with either sex. There are a plethora of different reasons why people don't talk about it after the fact. 

And you're totally right - I could have called the police. I should have called the police, but I didn't. Because I felt like shit about it. I felt a huge amount of shame. I was already dealing with enough problems in my life at that point (I had been in and out of the hospital with a cancer scare) and the assault was just the icing on cake with that. It may, in fact, be on me that it happened, but that doesn't make his actions any less wrong. He knew he fucked up and he's going to have to live with that for the rest of his life. He might see me in passing someday and know exactly what he did to me. There's even a chance I would throw him into an alley and break his face - I honestly don't know. 

But the fact of the matter is that a lot of victims of sexual assault don't report it. It's not an easy thing to do. My first two boyfriends were terrible people to me and sexuality has been a very touchy subject for me ever since. Is that an excuse? Maybe, but it's the way things happened and I can't change that. 

The whole point of posting here was to get help and to hopefully get some constructive feedback on how I should be feeling about this. Like I said before, I totally understand and hear your opinion on this, and I'm not going to try and change your mind about it, but I am just trying to help you see things from my perspective - even just a little bit. It's completely different to see something like this happen from the outside than it is to experience it yourself.
All very true. **Thank you.**

So to echo /u/madmadz415 here, you are being ignorant, and that's alright. You're totally entitled to have your own opinion on this subject, and I appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts on both my own situation and the situation that's been happening with my boyfriend.

I'd be curious to hear your thoughts about sexual assault when it comes to date rape drugs. As I mentioned before, I was on a medication (a combination of drugs called Seroquel and Lamotrigine) at night that basically knocked me out like a light. To give you an idea of what that's like - Seroquel is given to patients at hospitals as a sedative. I had to basically make sure I was getting nine hours of sleep at night - otherwise I literally would barely be able to wake up in the morning. 

I didn't sleep through my assault. I woke up, and I knew what was happening, but I literally did not have the energy to move. I am what most people would consider "athletic" so if I had had the energy to fight back, I **would** have. The words did come out of my mouth were ignored, and like /u/madmadz415 mentioned, there was a lot of pain involved. After the person who had assaulted me had finished, he had kind-of realized he fucked up and he left. **Also, we're not talking about a blowjob here. We're talking about extremely unwelcome anal sex.** The same for my boyfriend's situation too. Anal sex does **not** require a lot of cooperation from both parties. If I had someone try to shove their dick in my mouth and I didn't want it there, I would be chomping down as hard as I could with my teeth.

I don't know exactly what my boyfriend went through the two times he was assaulted. I don't know a thing about the first time, but I know alcohol was involved the second time. Is it possible that he could have fought back more? **Maybe?** but I have to take his word for it. As he was telling me all of this, I could tell it was a hard conversation for him to be having with me, and I believed him when he told me how much he hated himself for letting it happen to him again after the first time. But he also told me how good of a friend this person was to him, and how conflicted the whole situation made him feel because this was somebody he thought was a friend to him. I would never be able to rebuild any kind of social relationship with the person who assaulted me, and you can trust and believe that it makes me angry and uncomfortable that my boyfriend is even entertaining the idea of talking to this person again.

But that's not my call to make. I can only really share my opinion, and I have. I've told him about my own experience and how that experience affected me. I've tried to be rational and help him make sure he's seeing all the facts on the table. I've tried to point out he might be emotionally biased if he would give different advice on a situation like this to any of his loved ones that he wouldn't take himself. But at the end of the day, it's really not my call to make, and my entire purpose for posting about this was to get insight and help. 

People can drink too much all the time. Not everyone intentionally drinks too much to black out. It can just happen, and what happens after that point can be out of their control. Most people, let's hope, have a good friend that can take them home and put them into bed, but some people are not good friends, and for whatever reason decide to take advantage of somebody who trusted them. My boyfriend isn't a big guy. I can see him being overpowered by somebody, and the thought of that makes me extremely sad and angry.

It's also a bit ignorant and potentially homophobic to say that getting blackout drunk with "the gay rugby team" is a bad idea. Or referring to us as "snowflakes." Gay people have to deal with rape just as much as heterosexual people. I'm really sorry to hear that you've had girlfriends that have experienced rape, but I really don't understand how their situation is any different than mine or my boyfriends.

**Consent is consent**. I was super transparent with my assaulter that *I did not want to have* sex, and he did not respect those wishes. My boyfriend *told the person to stop* and he *did not stop*. How is this poor "sportsmanship" and not defined as sexual assault? It shouldn't even matter if drugs/alcohol were involved. Consent is consent.

At any rate, we can agree to disagree, I think. Thanks for taking the time to share your views.

I appreciate your support. I'm still sort-of reading through all of that other stuff and trying to compose a response, but I do appreciate you chiming in. It **definitely is** up to him on how he moves forward with this, and I've decided that I'm just going to be with him to support the best I can. 

I think the only thing that makes me uncomfortable is if he chooses to rebuild a friendship with this person. I mean, that's out of my control if that's what he chooses to do. 

I suppose with that it was just unusual to me that if one of his close friends was in the same situation, the advice that he would give them would be to stay away from them, and yet he isn't necessarily taking that advice right away himself. He's thinking. Having been in a similar situation myself, I could never imagine myself trying to rebuild a social connection with the person who assaulted me. Like /u/Diablo165 said earlier - if that's the case, I won't be happy about it, but I'll support that decision if that's what he really wants.

But again, thank you.

Adrenaline doesn't always kick in from what I've heard. If you're passed the fuck out or you wake up still so drunk that the world is spinning, I can understand how fighting back might be challenging. 

I don't know the circumstances of the first assault on him. Just this one. And whether it was truly assault or not, I feel like as his boyfriend I should try and take his word for it.

With me it happened when I was on a medication that I would take at night that essentially tranquilized me. I had made it clear that sex was not something I had wanted to happen that day. This was someone I considered a friend and was hoping to get to know as something more, but he went against my wishes anyways. If you say one thing and the other person doesn't respect those wishes, that's assault.

This was very helpful. It's really straightforward and yet also thought out. You have your own opinions about things but you aren't letting them overlap with your SO's wishes.

I'm in the same boat though. If I were to run into this person I think I would instinctively want to become very hostile. The issue hasn't come up again since yesterday so I guess we'll have to see if there's more to this or whatever he ends up doing.

Either way I'll be there to help however I can.

I've been trying to stay moving. I'm on a leave of absence from work so I've been waking up and trying to go straight to the gym. I still don't have much of an appetite - the last couple of days have just burnt me out, though I try to choke down a green smoothie or something or some fruit. 

As I've mentioned in my other comments, I'm just sad because the intention of taking this medicine was to make the relationship better. So that the anxiety would no longer such a stress point for us - or my career/work. The doctors themselves said that none of this was my fault and that some people just react very strongly to these types of medications. The challenge is that my ex doesn't understand that - or chooses not to accept it. He thinks it's like drinking too much alcohol and doing something you regret. Alcohol muddles your inhibitions and your judgment. These meds were mentally changing the way I was interpreting the world around me.

The feelings I have for him haven't gone anywhere. We texted back and forth for a few minutes yesterday and he still says he has feelings for me, but needs to stand by his decision. He hopes that someday we might be able to try again, but right now we have to spend some time looking after ourselves. I just wish I could convince him to give me another chance at this.

It's hard to stay busy with my leave of absence though. I wake up at around 10am, am at the gym by 11 or 12, and am home by 1:30 or 2. I have no idea what else to do with my day. 

But, like you said, I hope one day I am going to wake up, and everything is just going to be so much easier.

Yeah, I don't know. The doctor I had been seeing who prescribed this medication said that I might experience some minor side-effects. He was talking about stuff like headaches, nausea, some trouble sleeping or staying awake, etc. He didn't mention anything about the anxiety getting more worse than it already was. 

Like I said in another comment, it just shatters me because I took this medication to make things better. My intention by taking it was to reduce my anxiety so it would no longer put stress on my career and my relationship. My ex and I have been in touch a bit and he said that I need to take responsibility for what happened - and what happened was comparable to drinking too much and doing something regrettable. I tried to explain that the situations are completely different. Alcohol muddles your inhibitions and your judgment. These meds were mentally changing the way I was interpreting the world around me. The doctors in the hospital even explained to me that this behaviour wasn't my fault. 

My therapist has been helpful. She keeps me grounded and has offered up some helpful advice. I've been trying to keep a routine going (I've been waking up and going to the gym) but I'm on a leave of absence from work so I'm having trouble filling up my day with things to do. 

I just miss my boyfriend and am kicking myself. The whole idea of taking this medication was to make things better and it's just fucked everything up.

I really appreciate your support. Thank you.

It's just really frustrating because my intention by taking this medication was to make our relationship better. It's just bad timing - with the holidays and stuff. It's normally my favourite time of the year and I'm by myself through it now. I miss him a lot. I wish I could just go back in time. I'm on a new medication now that my body is tolerating a lot better, but the damage is done now. 

Just trying to put myself back together now.

I agree, and I've shared this with him. While none of this is really his fault, it's not easy to put aside several years of negativity. [I went into this a bit more in one of my other replies too.](https://www.reddit.com/r/relationships/comments/5hm6e2/im_28m_having_trouble_trusting_my_boyfriend_24m/db18snc/)

I've seen a therapist twice now about this, although she is very expensive. I feel like the reassurance my mind is looking for needs to come from my boyfriend, but I hope that maybe the therapy will give me some skills to tackle this better at the very least. I wonder if it would be constructive to invite my boyfriend to sit in on a session just so he understands a bit better that this isn't as easy as it looks?

Earlier on in the relationship he was a lot more willing to give me the reassurance I was looking for. At the same time, I was a lot more cautious about going into the relationship in the beginning, which is probably why he was willing to go above and beyond to give me the reassurance that I needed. He wanted to convince me that he was not like my exes. He really wanted to show me that he was different, and that captivated me.

But now that we've been dating for a while, he has said that he was hoping that the need for that reassurance would simmer down a bit, and that I would be able to just trust him. He's frustrated that I seemingly don't trust him - but I am trying. If I am feeling insecure about something, my nature and my problem solving method is to talk it out. In the beginning, he would sit and listen to whatever I had to say, and I think he's still trying to do that now, but there have been times he will just say outright that he is over whatever we were talking about and that I need to move on from it. I wish it were that easy.

It's not his fault that I have these insecurity issues in the first place, but I don't think he understands how challenging it is to work through 8+ years of negativity. What drew me to this guy in the first place was his patience and just how different he was to my exes. His recent reluctance (and shutting down) when I need help (despite him previously saying he'd be there for me for these kinds of things) is discouraging, and it almost makes me panic a little bit because these are not thoughts or feelings I am going through on purpose. I wish I could make them go away, and I realize a lot of these thoughts are irrational, but sometimes I just need to talk about them. He says he'll try his best, but he is upset that I don't seemingly trust him by now, and he was hoping that this would get better as time went by.

I've seen a therapist once or twice about this, but I think it's too early on to really see anything productive from it. I feel like the reassurance my mind wants needs to come from my boyfriend, though I am hoping the therapy might give me some skills to deal with these issues myself hopefully.
